Commercial rates and WMP content are edited the same way — this panel covers the two datasets that change most. Publishing regenerates waste_rates.json on R2 so the calculator and your Excel generator pick up changes immediately.
Council Guidelines — AI Extraction
Upload a council's waste guideline or DCP chapter (PDF). Enforceable requirements are extracted with clause and page references, reviewed here, then saved to a shared library — the compliance checker cites them by clause for every user scanning that council, on any device.
⇪ Drop guideline PDFs here (or click) — assign each file to its council below. Filenames are never auto-matched.
Each upload becomes a NEW version of that council's guideline — the previous version is superseded, and its structured requirements stop being served until a new extraction is approved.
Library
Requirements review queue
AI-proposed rows from guideline documents, each pinned to a document version and a clause reference. Verify each value against the cited clause, edit if needed, then approve — nothing is consumed by any tool until it is approved. Extraction confidence is not approval.

Registered Users

Equipment Library
Bins, compactors and chutes. The WMP spreadsheet reads these directly — after saving, hit Refresh All in Excel. No publish needed. A brand-new item also needs the spreadsheet block extended one row (copy the last formula row down).
AI Spec-Sheet Import
Upload a manufacturer spec sheet (PDF) — dimensions, capacities and contact details are extracted for review. Nothing touches the library until you accept each item, and every value stays editable before it lands.
Equipment proposals queue
Bulk spec-sheet extractions land here as proposals. Verify against the cited source, edit, set the permanent code, then approve to insert into the library. Streams, pairing, receiver and collectable are design decisions — set them in the table above after approval; a proposal can never carry them.
Plan-View Shape Editor
Every item gets geometry automatically from its profile (or an inferred one) scaled to its width/depth — this panel shows exactly what the layout tool and DXF will draw, and lets you override it. Paths are authored in a 0..1 unit box (front of the item = top). A pasted path always wins over the generated one; whatever the drawing's proportions, it is normalised to the row's real dimensions, so the artwork can never introduce a dimensional error.
Select an item to preview its plan-view shape
circle used for collision / keepouts instead of the path bounds
Contractors & Collection Vehicles
Collection services and vehicle dimensions. Same deal — Save here, Refresh All in Excel. New contractor = extend the spreadsheet block one row.
Swept path library: tick In swept lib to make a vehicle available in the swept path tool (needs wheelbase + kerb-to-kerb or wall-to-wall radius; wall-to-wall wins if both). Grouping is automatic: a Council value makes it council-specific (shown first for residential projects in that LGA); otherwise a Company makes it a contractor vehicle (commercial projects); neither = industry standard. Swept scope = residential / commercial / both. Austroads design vehicles live here too — swept tick on, contractor-table tick off. Swept changes feed the tool directly, no publish needed.
WMP Queue — client requests for certified plans
Each request arrives with the client's project snapshot. “Open in WMP Generator” loads it straight in — check every figure against the drawings before issuing.

Requests submitted under this organisation. Work belongs to the organisation — people are just assignees. Unassigned items, and items whose assignee has left, surface at the top.

Bin room layouts now live in the Workspace
Open a project, upload your plan and set the scale — then use the ⊞ Layout tab to draw bin rooms and place bins directly on the drawing, alongside the calculator and swept path tools. Layouts save with the project and export to DXF.
Submit to Council
Lodge a WMP with a council on WastePlanner. It lands in their review queue with a 7-day view link to your document — they see the submission, not your project.
Only councils with a WastePlanner account are listed. For any other council, lodge through the usual channel (e.g. the NSW Planning Portal) — a share link from the Documents card works there too.
Complete review
Close this request out and, optionally, send your response back to the submitter — comments, a marked-up document, an advice memo, or a certified WMP. It appears on their project.
Review completed ✓
The request is marked complete and the response is saved against the submitter's project. Document links are valid for 7 days — if you'd like to email them a copy as well:
